$comment: — Performance budgets. Bump baselines deliberately with the regressing PR; never silently. See docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md.

bundleSize.$comment: Per-chunk gzipped size ceiling in KB. Only chunks >= 5 KB gz are tracked here; smaller route splits and micro-icon chunks are noise. Chunk names strip the Rolldown content hash (e.g. SalesPage-Br3xY9Q_.js -> SalesPage).
bundleSize.$baseline: Captured from the Operator Deck Base 11 validation build, the recovery-ownership band on 2026-07-21, and the canonical product-payload and closed POS overlay splits on 2026-07-27. The shared index includes the typed control foundation; the design-system and operational-ownership boards stay route-split. Bilingual Operations copy and the product payload each own an explicit 8 kB ceiling.

trpcLatencyMs.$comment: p95 latency budget in milliseconds for a curated set of tRPC procedures. CI runs warmupIterations warmups then samplesPerProcedure measurements, computes p95, and asserts it falls within budget * (1 + thresholdPercent/100). Bias the procedure list toward routes the operator opens repeatedly during the day.

dataScale.$comment: Operator Deck live data-volume contract. The design-system route renders this many deterministic rows through the production DataTable; Playwright fails when the virtual window mounts more body rows than maxMountedRows.

storeProfile.$comment: Store-sized local SQLite contract. ci:server seeds the deterministic mega preset, proves minimum tenant row volumes, measures hot operational reads through the real tRPC caller, and pins the tenant-scoped indexes selected by SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.

productSearchProfile.$comment: C3/D1 search scale contract. ci:server grows one deterministic tenant catalog through 1k, 10k, and 50k products, checks FTS consistency and tenant isolation, measures the real products.search tRPC path for exact SKU, selective/broad FTS and substring fallback, and profiles the bounded 200-id hybrid semantic candidate pool without calling an AI provider.
productSearchProfile.$baseline: Broad-FTS baselines were recalibrated on 2026-08-13 from two sequential ubuntu-latest Backend Server runs for PR 197. The observed broad p95 maxima were 6.61 ms at 1k, 28.95 ms at 10k, and 136.50 ms at 50k; the 50k tier was reached in the first run because the second stopped at the earlier 10k assertion. Only this query shape changed: the existing 35% tolerance remains fixed and yields ceilings of 7.43, 32.40, and 148.50 ms. Re-capture serially on the hosted runner before changing these values again.

operationalProfile.$comment: Operator Deck Base 11. Store-scale write and desktop continuity budgets. Server CI measures the maximum supported launch-product import; desktop CI measures an encrypted backup round trip, built-runtime launch, and bounded database-lifecycle queue.

electronMemoryMb.$comment: Electron main + renderer working-set ceilings in MB, measured through app.getAppMetrics() by scripts/check-electron-memory.mjs. ci:desktop always uses --strict --require-measurement and fails on an absent measurement or a process above baseline plus threshold; only direct local diagnostic invocation remains warn-first unless those flags are supplied.
electronMemoryMb.$baseline: Captured locally on macOS and enforced on the Linux CI renderer. The 25% threshold is an explicit cross-platform working-set variance allowance, not permission to normalize the baseline upward; any measurement above the resulting ceiling fails ci:desktop.

longShiftSoak.$comment: Opt-in same-renderer leak contract. The web soak keeps one authenticated React tree alive, warms the finite route/query caches, then forces Chromium GC before each checkpoint. Ceilings apply only to retained final-minus-baseline growth; transient peaks are diagnostic, not leaks.

lighthouse.$comment: /  — Lighthouse web-vitals budgets per top user-facing route. ci:web runs scripts/run-lighthouse-gate.mjs, which seeds an isolated demo DB, serves an isolated web build, and invokes scripts/check-lighthouse.mjs with --strict --require-measurement so missing, statistically inconclusive, or over-budget proof fails push-CI. Each route uses the median of five complete audits; lcpMs/ttiMs in ms and cls use thresholdPercent, while score keeps its declared 0-100 floor with only scoreTolerancePoints of absolute shared-runner variance. When a five-sample score distribution is undecidable, meaning its IQR exceeds maxScoreIqrPoints and its range crosses the enforced floor, the gate extends that route to maxSamplesPerRoute complete audits and re-aggregates before judging; a final IQR above the cap still rejects evidence when the range crosses the floor, and conclusive same-side variance stays visible and unextended so extra samples can never turn a passing run into a rejection.
lighthouse.$baseline: — route floors remain anchored to the existing local production-preview baseline. Release-line evidence on the shared GitHub runner measured sales at 69, 71, and 72 around the declared 70 floor, including a 69/71 rerun pair for the same PR commit, while repeated local medians were 74-75. Five samples plus a two-point absolute score band absorbs that observed host variance without applying the unsafe 30% timing tolerance to score. On 2026-08-13 three hosted-runner runs across three branches were rejected as unstable (dashboard 59-76 and sales 63-74 spreads with medians 6-14 points above their floors) and every one passed a plain rerun, so a five-sample spread that is wide AND crosses the floor now extends to seven samples before judging instead of discarding the run. A final IQR above four points remains a blocking uncertainty only when the sample range crosses the enforced floor; otherwise it is reported as conclusive volatility. Re-capture deliberately with the isolated pnpm run ci:web path and retain the host plus per-sample diagnostics.
